title: Direct and Reported Speech
summary: How to punctuate direct speech, the four steps to change it into reported speech, reporting questions and commands, and when to use each one in your writing.

blocks.text: 1. Two ways to tell what someone said

**Direct speech** gives the speaker's exact words inside inverted commas. **Reported speech** (also called indirect speech) tells us what someone said **without** their exact words and **without** inverted commas. Reported speech is very useful in **news reports**, recounts and stories.

items: **Direct:** *Hana said, “I am tired.”*
**Reported:** *Hana said (that) she was tired.*
Put the spoken words inside **inverted commas**: “ ”.
Start the speech with a **capital letter**.
Put the **comma, full stop, question mark or exclamation mark inside** the closing inverted commas.
If the speaker comes first, put a **comma** before the opening inverted commas.
Start a **new line** every time a new person speaks.

rows: *“The bus is late,” said Omar, “so we will walk.”*

blocks.title: Small but important
blocks.text: After the closing inverted commas, the next word is usually small: *“Help!” **s**he cried.* ✓ not *“Help!” **S**he cried.* ✗ (unless it is a name: *“Help!” Mona cried.*)
3. Four steps to change direct speech into reported speech

items: **Remove the inverted commas.** You can add *that* (it is optional).
**Change the pronouns** to fit who is speaking: *I → he/she, we → they, my → his/her, our → their*.
**Move the tense one step back** if the reporting verb is in the past (*said, told, asked*).
**Change time and place words** if needed.

rows: past simple: He said he **played** chess.
past progressive: She said she **was reading**.
past perfect: He said he **had finished**.
past perfect: She said she **had seen** a fox.
had to: He said he **had to go**.
the day before / the previous day
the next day / the following day

blocks.title: Worked example
blocks.text: *“I will finish this drawing tomorrow,” said Malak.* → remove the inverted commas → *I* becomes *she* → *will* becomes *would* → *this* becomes *that*, *tomorrow* becomes *the next day*: ***Malak said (that) she would finish that drawing the next day.***

items: Yes/no question: *“Are you ready?” he asked.* → *He asked **if (whether)** I **was** ready.*
Wh- question: *“Where do you live?” she asked.* → *She asked where I **lived**.* (no question mark, normal word order)
Command: *“Sit down,” the teacher said.* → *The teacher **told** us **to sit** down.*
Negative command: *“Don't run!” Mum said.* → *Mum told us **not to run**.*

blocks.title: Said or told?
blocks.text: **told** needs a person after it: *She **told me** that...* ✓. **said** does not: *She **said** that...* ✓. So *She said me...* ✗ and *She told that...* ✗.

blocks.title: No backshift needed
blocks.text: If the reporting verb is in the present (*says, tells*), the tense does not change: *Ali says, “I am hungry.”* → *Ali says he is hungry.* The tense also usually stays the same for facts that are always true: *She said the Nile flows north.*
Instead of *said* every time, choose a verb that shows **how** something was said. This also helps your **Vocabulary and language** mark.

rows: spoke very loudly, maybe in fear or anger
said they would definitely do something

blocks.title: Watch out for these
items: Keeping the inverted commas: *He said that “he was tired.”* ✗ → *He said that he was tired.* ✓
Forgetting the pronoun: *Sara said that I was hungry* ✗ (when Sara meant herself) → *Sara said that **she** was hungry* ✓
Question word order: *She asked where did I live?* ✗ → *She asked where I **lived**.* ✓
*He told that he was late* ✗ → *He **said** that he was late* / *He **told me** that he was late* ✓
Punctuation outside: *“Stop”, she said* ✗ → *“Stop,” she said* ✓

blocks.title: Reading questions in this style
items: *Why does the writer use direct speech here?* → to show the character's feelings or personality, to make the scene lively and real, or to move the story on through dialogue.
In a news report: *Why does the writer include the words of a witness?* → to make the report believable and give a real person's view.
*What does the verb “whispered” tell you about the character?* → they were scared, secretive or did not want to be heard.
Questions on punctuation can ask why inverted commas are used: they show the exact words someone spoke.

blocks.text: **In your writing:** in stories, a **few** lines of well-punctuated dialogue bring characters to life, but too much speech slows the story. In **news reports**, mix one direct quote from a witness with reported speech:

items: *“I heard a loud crash and ran outside,” said shop owner Karim Fathy.* (direct)
*Police said that nobody had been hurt.* (reported)

blocks.title: نصيحة سريعة
items: في الكلام المنقول: شيل علامات التنصيص، غيّر الضمائر، ارجع بالزمن خطوة لورا، وغيّر كلمات الزمان والمكان.
told لازم بعدها شخص (told me / told us)، لكن said لأ.
السؤال المنقول بيبقى زي الجملة العادية: من غير علامة استفهام ومن غير do/did.

items.q: Report it: *“I am going to the market,” said Mum.*
items.a: *Mum said (that) she was going to the market.*

items.q: Report it: *“We have finished the project,” the boys said.*
items.a: *The boys said (that) they had finished the project.*

items.q: Report it: *“Will you help me tomorrow?” Ali asked his brother.*
items.a: *Ali asked his brother if (whether) he would help him the next day.*

items.q: Report it: *“Don't touch the oven!” Grandma told us.*
items.a: *Grandma told us not to touch the oven.*

items.q: Change to direct speech: *The coach said that the match had been cancelled.*
items.a: *The coach said, “The match has been cancelled.”*

items.q: Add the missing punctuation: *where are my keys asked Dad*
Report it: *“What time does the film start?” Nada asked.*
items.a: *Nada asked what time the film started.*

items.q: Report it: *“I can't find my homework,” said Youssef.*
items.a: *Youssef said (that) he couldn't find his homework.*

items.q: Correct the mistake: *The teacher said us to open our books.*
items.a: *The teacher **told** us to open our books.*

items.q: Choose a better reporting verb for a frightened character: *“Is someone there?” she ______.*
items.a: ***whispered*** (or *stammered*), which shows she is scared and speaking quietly.
